articles.title: Sean 'Diddy' Combs trial live updates: Cassie Ventura returns to the witness stand for day 2 of cross-examination - Yahoo
articles.description: The 55-year-old hip-hop mogul has been charged by federal prosecutors with sex trafficking, racketeering conspiracy and transportation to engage in...
articles.content: Sean 'Diddy' Combs trial live updates: Week 1 wraps up in the sex trafficking caseSearch querySearch the webSkip to mainNewsFinanceSportsMoreManage your accountHelpAdd or switch accountsSign outSearch the webAdvertisementAdvertisementAdvertisementReturn to HomepageTop Stories: What We Inherit From Our ParentsHow Colin Jost Became a JokeTrump’s Transactional Foreign PolicyThe Neo-Anti-Vaxxers Are in Power NowNo One Knows How to ‘Save’ HollywoodWhy Are There So Many ‘Alternative Devices’ All of a Sudden?The Supreme Court just got an important police violence case rightSilencing Voice of AmericaThe Good News About CrimeThe Question the Trump Administration Couldn’t Answer About Birthright CitizenshipLiveSean 'Diddy' Combs trial live updates: Week 1 wraps up in the sex trafficking caseFederal prosecutors say the hip-hop mogul coerced multiple women to participate in "freak offs," drug-fueled sex encounters that lasted for days.Dylan Stableford, Kate Murphy, Katie MatherUpdated Fri, May 16, 2025 at 9:24 PM UTCLawyer Anna Estevao cross-examines Cassie Ventura as Judge Arun Subramanian and Sean "Diddy" Combs' look on Friday in this courtroom sketch. (Jane Rosenberg/Reuters)The trial of Sean “Diddy” Combs wrapped up its first week late Friday afternoon in Manhattan federal court. Cassie Ventura, his former girlfriend and the prosecution’s star witness, finished up her testimony after four days on the witness stand in the high-profile sex trafficking case.Over the last week, federal prosecutors have begun to lay out their case that, for decades, Combs abused, threatened and coerced women to participate in marathon sexual encounters called "freak offs" and used his business empire, along with guns, kidnapping and arson, to conceal his crimes. The 55-year-old hip-hop mogul is facing charges of sex trafficking, racketeering conspiracy and transportation to engage in prostitution.Testifying for more than 20 hours this week, Ventura — who is eight months pregnant — told the court her decade-long relationship with Combs was frequently marked by violence and physical abuse, describing in detail the drug-fueled "freak offs" that would take days to recover from. Jurors were also shown a 2016 surveillance video of Combs hitting, kicking and dragging Ventura in the hallway of a Los Angeles hotel.AdvertisementAdvertisementAdvertisementAdvertisementThe defense team presented hundreds of text messages between Ventura and Combs from throughout their relationship in an attempt to show that Ventura was a consensual participant in the "freak offs," sometimes even planning them herself.Two more witnesses testified Friday after Ventura, including a special agent with Homeland Security Investigations who took part in searches related to the Combs investigation and his September 2024 arrest, and singer Dawn Richard, who was part of the singing group Danity Kane formed by Combs. Richard testified that she witnessed Combs physically assault Ventura on multiple occasions.Combs has pleaded not guilty. If convicted, he could face life in prison. He is being held without bail in a Brooklyn jail. A jury of 12 New Yorkers and six alternates will decide his fate. The trial is expected to last at least eight weeks.Follow the live blog below for the latest updates on the trial, culled from various reporters and news organizations in the courtroom, including the Associated Press, CNN, the New York Times and NBC News.If you or someone you know is experiencing domestic violence, you can call the National Domestic Violence Hotline at 1-800-799-SAFE (7233). Find more resources here.Live156 updatesFri, May 16, 2025 at 5:13 PM EDTKatie MatherCourt concludes for the week, jurors will return Monday morningCassie Ventura cries on the stand during redirect as Judge Arun Subramanian presides Sean Combs's sex trafficking trial in New York City on May 16, in this courtroom sketch. (Jane Rosenberg/Reuters)Judge Arun Subramanian dismissed the jury for the day, concluding the first full week of Sean Combs's trial. Combs faces five criminal charges and has pleaded not guilty to sex trafficking, racketeering conspiracy and transportation to engage in prostitution. If convicted on all counts, he could face life in prison.Cassie Ventura, Combs's ex-girlfriend, testified for nearly 20 hours over the last four days about her relationship with Combs, which lasted over 10 years.After Ventura was excused from the witness stand on Friday afternoon, the prosecution called on Special Agent Yasin Binda and former Danity Kane singer Dawn Richard as the next two witnesses.Jurors are expected to return to court Monday morning.Fri, May 16, 2025 at 5:05 PM EDTKatie MatherRichard testifies that she saw Combs attack Ventura in 2009Dawn Richard testified that she worked for Sean Combs between 2004 and 2011, and she saw Combs act violently toward Cassie Ventura.She described one specific instance in 2009. Richard said she was at Combs's home recording when “he came downstairs screaming, belligerent, asking where his food was, and proceeded to hit her over the head, kicked her and beat her to the ground in front of us." Richard said Combs then dragged Ventura up the stairs by her hair, and she could hear "glass breaking and yelling" upstairs.Richard said she didn't call the police or try to intervene because she was "scared to do anything in fear of what that might mean for me too."Fri, May 16, 2025 at 4:47 PM EDTKatie MatherWho is Dawn Richard? Former Danity Kane singer takes the stand to testify against Combs.Sean Combs with pop group Danity Kane in August 2007. Dawn Richard is at far left. (Scott Gries/Getty Images)Dawn Richard, one of the singers of the girl group Danity Kane, has taken the witness stand.Richard was a contestant on the third season (2004) of Combs's MTV show Making the Band, which led to Danity Kane forming and signing with Combs's Bad Boy Records label in 2005. After Danity Kane went on hiatus in 2009, Richard joined a trio with Combs and singer Kalenna Harper called Diddy — Dirty Money.In September 2024, Richard filed a lawsuit against Combs, accusing him of threatening her, touching her inappropriately and flying into "frenzied, unpredictable rages" when he was in charge of her musical career. In the lawsuit, Richard said there were times when Combs would order her to strip down to her underwear, throw objects at her or fail to pay her for her time and work.Richard's lawsuit also said there were several occasions where she witnessed Combs physically abuse Ventura, and tried to intervene.Fri, May 16, 2025 at 4:46 PM EDTKatie MatherDefense cross-examines special agent about Combs's NYC hotel roomAfter prosecutor Madison Smyser finished questioning special agent Yasin Binda, defense attorney Teny Geragos stood to cross-examine her.Binda testified that it did appear a woman was staying with Combs in the Manhattan hotel room before he was arrested in 2024.After confirming the detail, Binda left the stand.AdvertisementAdvertisementFri, May 16, 2025 at 4:38 PM EDTKatie MatherJury sees photos of hotel room where Combs was staying when he was arrested in September 2024The jury was shown photos taken by Special Agent Yasin Binda when law enforcement searched Sean Combs's New York City hotel room after his September 2024 arrest. He had been staying in Room 2115 at the Park Hyatt Hotel.The photos showed Ziploc bags of baby oil and lubricant, which were pulled from a closet. More baby oil and lubricant were found in the bathroom.There was also a photo of a lighting device found in the living room, which Binda testified was "potentially mood lighting."Photos of the bedroom showed a bottle of clonazepam and two small bags of pink powder. Binda said one of the pink powder bags tested positive for ketamine, and the other tested positive for ketamine and MDMA. Binda also said agents found a black fanny pack hanging off the bed, which contained $9,000 in cash.Fri, May 16, 2025 at 4:19 PM EDTKatie MatherProsecution calls new witness to the standHomeland Security Investigations Special Agent Yasin Binda has now taken the witness stand.Binda, who works for the department's human trafficking division, helped coordinate logistics for Sean Combs's arrest in September 2024 and was involved in searches related to the investigation.Fri, May 16, 2025 at 3:50 PM EDTKate MurphyVentura issues statement saying this week has been 'remarkably empowering and healing' for herDougl Wigdor, Cassie Ventura's attorney, read the following statement from Ventura to reporters outside the Manhattan courthouse moments after she finished testifying:“This week has been extremely challenging, but also remarkably empowering and healing for me. I hope that my testimony has given strength and a voice to other survivors, and can help others who have suffered to speak up and also heal from the abuse and fear.For me, the more I heal, the more I can remember. And the more I can remember, the more I will never forget. I want to thank my family and my advocates for their unwavering support, and I’m grateful for all the kindness and encouragement that I have received.I’m glad to put this chapter of my life to rest. As I turn to focus on the conclusion of my pregnancy, I ask for privacy for me and for my growing family.”Fri, May 16, 2025 at 3:37 PM EDTKatie MatherVentura reveals she's set to receive around $10M settlement from L.A. hotel over 2016 assaultBefore Ventura was excused from the witness stand, she told the court that her legal team is still negotiating a settlement with the InterContinental Hotel after Combs assaulted her in a hallway there in 2016.A deal has not yet been struck, but Ventura estimated under cross-examination that it would be around $10 million. She did not disclose the specifics of her claim against the hotel.AdvertisementAdvertisementFri, May 16, 2025 at 3:26 PM EDTKate MurphyCassie Ventura wraps up her testimony; court takes a breakCassie Ventura, Combs's ex-girlfriend, has finished testifying in his sex trafficking trial. The court is taking a break before the next witness is called.Fri, May 16, 2025 at 3:15 PM EDTKatie MatherDefense asks Ventura to confirm Combs let her end contract with Bad Boy RecordsDefense attorney Anna Estevao asked Cassie Ventura to confirm that Combs ultimately allowed her to end her recording contract with Bad Boy Records, Combs's music label, when their relationship ended in 2018."I had to fight my way out of the contract," Ventura responded, adding that she eventually was able to end the contract with Bad Boy Records.Fri, May 16, 2025 at 3:14 PM EDTKatie MatherVentura testifies she'd give back $20M settlement 'if I never had to have "freak offs"'Prosecutor Emily Johnson asked Ventura about the lawsuit she settled with Combs in 2023. Ventura previously testified that Combs gave her $20 million in the settlement, and the defense had just tried to suggest the settlement alleviated all of her financial concerns, which is why she canceled her music tour in 2023.Johnson asked Ventura if she'd return the settlement if it meant she never had to experience "freak offs" in the first place."I'd give that money back if I never had to have 'freak offs,'" Ventura said. "If I never had to have 'freak offs,' I would have had agency and autonomy. I wouldn't have had to work so hard to get it back."Fri, May 16, 2025 at 2:58 PM EDTDylan StablefordVentura is asked about timeline surrounding alleged rapeDuring cross-examination, Ventura was questioned about inconsistencies in the timeline of events surrounding her rape allegation against Combs.In court, Ventura said the attack occurred in August 2018. But in her 2023 civil lawsuit, Ventura said the alleged incident took place in September of that year.During redirect, prosecutor Emily Johnson asked about the discrepancy.Ventura acknowledged her memory of that period was "not super clear, but clear enough.”“Do you have any doubt that Sean raped you?” Johnson asked.“No,” Ventura replied.AdvertisementAdvertisementFri, May 16, 2025 at 2:48 PM EDTKatie MatherProsecution asks Ventura to testify about what happened at L.A. hotel in March 2016The prosecution revisited the events of March 5, 2016, when Sean Combs assaulted Cassie Ventura at the InterContinental Hotel in Los Angeles."He followed me into the hallway and tried to bring me back," Ventura testified. The prosecution has been trying to demonstrate that Combs physically dragged Ventura back to the hotel room where a "freak off" was happening in March 2016.Fri, May 16, 2025 at 2:46 PM EDTDylan StablefordVentura considered herself a 'sex worker,' but judge tells jury to disregard that statementBefore she began dating Combs, Ventura signed a 10-album contract with Combs's record label. But the R&B singer said Friday that the "freak offs" with him took precedence."I had a whole other job, basically a sex worker," Ventura told the court.The defense objected to the characterization, and Judge Arun Subramanian told jurors to disregard the statement.Fri, May 16, 2025 at 2:28 PM EDTDylan StablefordCombs is seen smiling and hugging his attorney in courtSean Combs embraces his lawyer Anna Estevao as he enters the courtroom on Friday. (Jane Rosenberg/Reuters)Because no photos or video of the trial are allowed under federal court rules, the public doesn't get to see the demeanor of the judge, lawyers, witnesses or the defendant for itself. But we have gotten a few glimpses courtesy of sketch artists like Jane Rosenberg, who has depicted a relaxed Sean Combs smiling and hugging his attorney Anna Estevao and earlier this week making the sign of a heart to family members.In a courtroom sketch, Combs makes a hand gesture to family members arriving at his sex trafficking trial in New York City on Tuesday. (Jane Rosenberg/Reuters)Fri, May 16, 2025 at 2:27 PM EDTKatie MatherProsecution revisits parts of Ventura's testimony in redirectProsecutor Emily Johnson is now questioning specific points of Ventura's testimony, including the recording the defense played of her threatening someone who claimed to have seen a sexually explicit video of her in 2014. In the recording, Ventura had threatened to kill the man involved."I was just sick about it and was feeling pressure from Sean," Ventura told Johnson. "It was a weird day."AdvertisementAdvertisementFri, May 16, 2025 at 2:09 PM EDTDylan StablefordDefense ends its cross-examination of VenturaThe defense team ended its cross-examination of Ventura shortly after returning from lunch.Prosecutor Emily Johnson has begun what she earlier indicated would be a half-hour of follow-up questions, known as a redirect.Defense Anna Estevao concluded her questioning by Ventura asking her to read a text message exchange she had with Combs from September 2012.In it, Combs asked her if she wanted to engage in a "freak off" for "one last time."Ventura replied: “I don’t want to freak off for the last time. I want it to be the first time for the rest of our lives.”Estevao ended her cross-examination there, but Johnson had Ventura read more messages from the exchange.“I want to see you, but I’m emotional right now,” Ventura wrote to Combs. “I don’t want to do one last time. I’d rather not do it at all.”Fri, May 16, 2025 at 1:32 PM EDTDylan StablefordCassie Ventura returns to the witness standAfter a lunch break, CassieVentura returned to the witness stand for more cross-examination by the defense.Ventura, who is eight months pregnant, has spent more than 20 hours testifying over the last four days.Judge Arun Subramanian has told both sides he wants her testimony to conclude today.“We’re almost finished here,” defense lawyer Anna Estevao told Ventura after she returned to the stand.“Thank you,” Ventura replied.Fri, May 16, 2025 at 1:14 PM EDTKatie MatherA spokesperson for Justin Bieber issues statement on relationship with CombsSean Combs, left, and Justin Bieber perform at the BET-SOS Saving Ourselves Benefit Concert on Feb. 5, 2010, in Miami. (Getty Images)Outside of the courtroom, a spokesperson for Justin Bieber released a statement on Thursday to make clear that the singer wasn't "among Sean Combs' victims."Bieber, 31, has stayed quiet regarding Combs's arrest and the accusations against him, which sparked online commentators to question whether Bieber may have been involved. Bieber and Combs have publicly collaborated as far back as 2009, when Bieber was 15 years old and Combs was 40."Although Justin is not among Sean Combs' victims, there are individuals who were genuinely harmed by him," Bieber's spokesperson said. "Shifting focus away from this reality detracts from the justice these victims rightfully deserve."Fri, May 16, 2025 at 12:59 PM EDTDylan StablefordVentura says she doesn't 'hate' CombsDuring Friday's cross-examination, Ventura was asked by defense attorney Anna Estevao if she still had feelings for Combs, even after he allegedly raped her in August 2018.“You didn’t hate him then. And you don’t still hate him now,” Estevao said.“I don’t hate him,” Ventura said.“You still have love for him?” Estevao asked.“I have love for the past, what it was,” Ventura replied.Show more updatesAdvertisementAbout Our AdsSolve the daily Crossword33,623 people played the daily Crossword recently. articles.title: Man who attacked author Salman Rushdie is sentenced to 25 years in prison - NPR
articles.description: Hadi Matar got the maximum sentence for attempted murder. He was found guilty in February for repeatedly stabbing author Salman Rushdie during a 2022 lecture and wounding another person on stage.
articles.content: Man who attacked author Salman Rushdie gets 25 years in prison : NPR Accessibility links Skip to main content Keyboard shortcuts for audio player Open Navigation Menu Newsletters NPR Shop Close Navigation Menu Home News Expand/collapse submenu for News National World Politics Business Health Science Climate Race Culture Expand/collapse submenu for Culture Books Movies Television Pop Culture Food Art & Design Performing Arts Life Kit Gaming Music Expand/collapse submenu for Music All Songs Considered Tiny Desk New Music Friday Music Features Live Sessions Podcasts & Shows Expand/collapse submenu for Podcasts & Shows Daily Morning Edition Weekend Edition Saturday Weekend Edition Sunday All Things Considered Fresh Air Up First Featured Embedded The NPR Politics Podcast Throughline Trump's Terms More Podcasts & Shows Search Newsletters NPR Shop All Songs Considered Tiny Desk New Music Friday Music Features Live Sessions About NPR Diversity Support Careers Press Ethics Man who attacked author Salman Rushdie gets 25 years in prison Hadi Matar got the maximum sentence for attempted murder. He was found guilty in February for repeatedly stabbing author Salman Rushdie during a 2022 lecture and wounding another person on stage. National Man who attacked author Salman Rushdie is sentenced to 25 years in prison Updated May 16, 202511:48 AM ET Originally published May 16, 202510:57 AM ET By Scott Neuman Novelist Salman Rushdie promotes the German-language edition of his book Knife: Meditations After an Attempted Murder in Berlin on May 16, 2024. In the book, Rushdie confronts the 2022 attack that left him blind in one eye. Sean Gallup/Getty Images hide caption toggle caption Sean Gallup/Getty Images Hadi Matar, the man who severely injured novelist Salman Rushdie in a 2022 stabbing attack, was sentenced Friday to 25 years in prison — the maximum for attempted murder. National Man who stabbed Salman Rushdie convicted of attempted murder Matar, 27, was found guilty of second-degree attempted murder in February for his attack on the author at the nonprofit Chautauqua Institution in New York state in August 2022. A knife-wielding Matar leapt onto the stage where Rushdie was about to give a lecture, stabbing the author multiple times in the face, neck, arm, abdomen and eye. The assault left Rushdie, now 77, partially blind and with permanent nerve damage. The author did not return to the Chautauqua County court in Mayville, N.Y., for the sentencing, but did submit a victim impact statement. Sponsor Message Judge David Foley also sentenced Matar to 7 years, to be served concurrently, for injuring the moderator who tried to stop the attack. Hadi Matar (right) and public defender Nathaniel Barone listen to Chautauqua County Judge David Foley's sentence in Chautauqua County court in Mayville, N.Y., on Friday. Adrian Kraus/AP hide caption toggle caption Adrian Kraus/AP Rushdie's book The Satanic Verses, published in 1988, sparked angry protests in the Muslim world over its controversial depiction of the life of the Prophet Muhammad. Months before his death in 1989, Iran's Supreme Leader, the Ayatollah Khomeini, issued a religious fatwa calling for Rushdie's murder. Author Interviews Two nights before the attack, Salman Rushdie dreamed he was stabbed onstage At trial, the U.S. Attorney's Office for the Western District of New York alleged Matar was acting on the fatwa. Matar, who lived in Fairview, N.J., at the time of the attack, has not cited the religious decree as motivation, but has said he disliked Rushdie, telling the New York Post in a jailhouse interview that the author had attacked Islam. In the same interview, Matar admitted that he had read only about two pages of The Satanic Verses. Rushdie himself testified at the February trial, telling the jury that the assailant struck him repeatedly. The novelist described being taken by surprise in the attack and then suddenly becoming aware of "a very large quantity of blood pouring out onto my clothes." Matar's defense team argued that it wasn't an open-and-shut case. "Something very bad did happen," attorney Lynn Schaffer acknowledged at the trial, adding that the prosecution was required "to prove much more than that." Sponsor Message Matar also faces federal terrorism charges Matar faces a separate trial on federal charges of terrorism in connection with the attack on Rushdie. When the charges were filed last July, then-FBI Director Christopher Wray said Matar "attempted to carry out a fatwa endorsed by [Hezbollah] that called for the death of Salman Rushdie — a fatwa issued in 1989 by Iran's Ayatollah Khomeini." If convicted on the federal charges — which include providing material support to terrorists and conspiracy to kill a U.S. citizen — Matar faces life in prison. A trial date hasn't been set. The award-winning Rushdie, who is an Indian-born British-American citizen, has written numerous books. Besides The Satanic Verses, he is also author of Midnight's Children, set in postcolonial India, and Knife: Meditations After an Attempted Murder, a memoir about the attack that was published last year. Correction May 16, 2025 A previous version of this story incorrectly said Hadi Matar was found guilty of second-degree murder. In fact, he was convicted of second-degree attempted murder. salman rushdie Literature Facebook Flipboard Email Read & Listen Home News Culture Music Podcasts & Shows Connect Newsletters Facebook Instagram Press Public Editor Corrections Contact & Help About NPR Overview Diversity NPR Network Accessibility Ethics Finances Get Involved Support Public Radio Sponsor NPR NPR Careers NPR Shop NPR Events NPR Extra Terms of Use Privacy Your Privacy Choices Text Only Sponsor Message Sponsor MessageBecome an NPR sponsor

Associated Press 2 minute read Updated 10:43 AM EDT, Fri May 16, 2025 Link Copied! Follow: People in entertainment See your latest updates US singer Chris Brown, pictured in May 2023 in Las Vegas was remanded into custody in a British courtroom on Friday. Matt Baron/BEI/Shutterstock AP — Grammy-winning singer Chris Brown’s upcoming tour was thrown into question Friday as a British judge ordered him held in custody while facing allegations that he beat a music producer with a bottle in a London nightclub in 2023. Brown, 36, appeared in Manchester Magistrates’ Court to face one count of causing grievous bodily harm and was ordered held until his next hearing June 13 in London – the same day he’s due to take the stage in Frankfurt, Germany, on the third date of his world tour. Judge Joanne Hirst rejected Brown’s bail request after prosecutor Hannah Nicholls said that the crime was “extremely serious.” Brown was on tour in the UK in February 2023 when he is alleged to have attacked producer Abe Diaw with a bottle at the Tape nightclub, in London’s Mayfair neighborhood. Defense attorney Grace Forbes argued that the American performer wasn’t a flight risk and should be released. Brown was flanked by court officers in the dock. His hair was bleached blonde and he wore sweatpants and a black T-shirt. He confirmed his name and birth date, and said that his address was the local Lowry Hotel, where he was arrested early Thursday and taken into custody. His case was transferred to Southwark Crown Court in London, where he is expected to enter a plea to the charge. Brown’s representative didn’t immediately respond to a request for comment from The Associated Press. Brown, often called by his nickname Breezy, burst onto the music scene as a teen in 2005 and has become a major hitmaker over the years with notable songs such as “Run It,” “Kiss Kiss” and “Without You.” He won his first Grammy for best R&B album in 2011 for “F.A.M.E.” and then earned his second gold trophy in the same category for “11:11 (Deluxe)” earlier this year. The singer is due to launch an international tour next month with artists Jhene Aiko, Summer Walker and Bryson Tiller, opening with a European leg on June 8 in Amsterdam before starting North America shows in July. President Donald Trump on Friday morning chose to announce that Taylor Swift is no longer 'HOT'. He also analyzed the reason why this happened: because he said that he hated Taylor Swift. While MAGA activists cheered and they said they voted for this, early morning pearls of wisdom from the president dissing liberal Taylor Swift -- Swifties are enraged. Trump was a fan of Taylor Swift and called her 'fantastic' and 'terrific' but that changed after Taylor Swift became politically vocal and sided with the Democrats with strong criticism for Trump and Vice President JD Vance this election.Donald Trump vs Taylor SwiftIn 2028, Donald Trump said he liked Taylor Swift 25 per cent less after she endorsed Democratic candidates Phil Bredesen and Jim Cooper in Tennesseeâs midterm elections. This became 100 per cent in 2024, after Trump posted AI-generated images on Truth Social, falsely suggesting Swift endorsed him. âTaylor wants you to vote for Donald Trump," Trump wrote.Taylor Swift responded by endorsing Kamala Harris on Instagram, citing the fake images as a reason to clarify her stance, calling Harris a âsteady-handed, gifted leaderâ and signing off as âChildless Cat Ladyâ in a jab at Vance. Trump retaliated on Truth Social with an all-caps post: âI HATE TAYLOR SWIFT!â This outburst drew backlash from Swiftâs fans and public figures like Liz Cheney, who referenced Swiftâs song âThe Smallest Man Who Ever Livedâ in her response.In February this year, both Trump and Taylor Swift attended the Super Bowl LIX. Taylor was there to support her boyfriend, Kansas City Chiefs tight end Travis Kelce, but she was booed by some in the crowd while there were loud cheers for Trump. Trump seized the moment, posting on Truth Social, âThe only one that had a tougher night than the Kansas City Chiefs was Taylor Swift. She got BOOED out of the Stadium. MAGA is very unforgiving!â He shared videos contrasting his cheers with her boos, though fans noted Trump was also booed at the event.
